patch_description:
Key ideas:
- Reduce parameter count per block to 13 (78 total) by exploiting tic-tac-toe symmetries: corners share, edges share, center treated separately. This improves parameter efficiency and reduces overfitting.
- Split grid CRZ couplings into two shared parameters: crz_ring for the eight outer-ring edges and crz_center_edge for the four spokes to the center. This gives the optimizer explicit control over perimeter vs hub correlations.
- Include ZZZ (three-qubit) rotations aligned with the eight winning lines (rows, columns, diagonals) grouped into three shared parameters (row/col/diag) to directly encode higher-order motifs relevant to the task.
- Use CCRZ (doubly-controlled RZ) interactions split by geometry (edge-edge-center vs corner-corner-center) to provide additional expressive, motif-aligned nonlinearity at low parameter cost.
- Finish with symmetry-grouped RZ rotations to allow final phase adjustments.

This configuration mirrors the best prior seed (78 params) but emphasizes the perimeter/spoke CRZ split and motif-aligned triple interactions. Fewer parameters, structured sharing, and geometry-aligned three-body gates improve generalization and parameter efficiency while keeping expressivity for the tic-tac-toe classification task.
